newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Switzerland offers to create Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Switzerland offers to create Holocaust fund.

text.p: The Swiss government, pressured by Jewish groups to make restitution for alleged Swiss profiteering from the Holocaust, said on Tuesday it wanted to use dormant Swiss bank accounts to create a Holocaust memorial fund.

But a Jewish leader in Israel rebuffed the move, saying he would decide in four weeks whether to call for a boycott of Swiss banks in response to a Swiss minister's complaint that his country was being "blackmailed" over the issue.
"They're trying to buy us with money that's not theirs," said Jewish Agency chairman Avraham Burg.
Switzerland's Federal Council, or cabinet, ignored demands that it rebuke Economics Minister Jean-Pascal Delamuraz for dismissing calls for compensation as "extortion and blackmail".
"There was no apology by the Federal Council because the remarks were misunderstood and led to excessive reactions," government spokesman Achille Casanova told reporters.
The cabinet said the threats of a boycott endangered joint efforts to track Jewish wealth sent to neutral Switzerland to escape the Nazis during World War Two.
It said it wanted dormant accounts totalling about 40 million Swiss francs ($29 million) to be "put to a proper use".

"The Federal Council is ready to immediately take up discussions with the banks and the interested organisations regarding the creation of a fund in favour of Holocaust victims and their descendants," its statement said.
The government denies that would be an admission Switzerland and its secretive banks profited cynically from the war.
It left open potential compensation for Jews but only if a probe by historians proves Switzerland acted dishonourably.

Burg said he would not take part in any search for dormant accounts by a joint Swiss-Jewish commission headed by former U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Paul Volcker unless members of the committee denounced Delamuraz's comments.
"It will be almost impossible for us to sit together around the same table with people who did not deny, did not regret and did not oppose the president calling me a blackmailer," he said.

"We are going to settle once and forever the moral and economic commitment that we have to families, fathers, mothers who have perished in the Holocaust," he said, adding his grandmother was among six million Jews killed by the Nazis.
"Not even one dime or dollar or Swiss franc...which was done in an unjust way will remain in their safety vaults."
Swiss bank shares fell on Monday in what some traders said was a response to the calls for a boycott.
Berne's top official handling the issue, Thomas Borer, said the government expected to decide by the end of January whether to create a memorial fund.

The Swiss Bankers Association hailed the proposal for talks, but said the Volcker commission should first rule on how much of the money stemmed from Jews killed in the Holocaust -- a conclusion expected in mid-1998.
Bankers say not all accounts belonged to victims of the Nazis and efforts to match funds with claims had traced only 11,000 Swiss francs to Jewish owners by last November.
The bankers association said no money could be used for a fund until all valid claims had been ruled out for each account.

The Swiss National Bank (SNB), Switzerland's central bank, on Tuesday denied allegations that the Swiss encouraged Nazi Germany to restamp looted gold bars to hide their origin, saying its own investigations had uncovered no evidence to back them.

Poland said meanwhile its former communist rulers had used money left in Swiss banks by Poles who died in World War Two, including Jews killed in the Holocaust, as compensation for assets seized by the communists in postwar years, and announced plans to identify the rightful heirs.
Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati said 16,000 Swiss francs from such accounts had gone to compensate Swiss claimants, while 464,000 francs had been paid into the 1975 Polish budget.
It is likely that many of the unclaimed Polish accounts were opened by Jews. Most of Poland's 3.5 million Jewish community were killed by the Nazis.
